title: Migrate hand-rolled auth and UI surfaces onto the shared ui layer
problem: 44 hand-written login/register/logout page files are spread across 17 repositories, and 22 repositories each implement their own theme switching. Meanwhile dotnet-platform-libs/ui is a complete, tested design-token and component layer whose adoption count is zero. The workspace pays for the same pages repeatedly and has no single place to change them.

evidence.counted_by: find/grep across /home/paul/code, excluding target, node_modules, obj, bin, dist, build, coverage, *.test.*, *.spec.*, e2e, and tests/

assets_already_present: ui/tokens/tokens.json — single DTCG token source, light and dark
ui/scripts/generate-tokens.mjs — generator, no code change needed to add a token
ui/scripts/verify-ui.mjs — accessibility oracle; fails on orphan color literals
ui/scripts/pack-ui.mjs — deterministic npm-pack equivalent writing feed/*.tgz
ui/packages/react-ui — Button, Field, Card, Badge, State, Dialog, Pagination
ui/packages/react-auth — LoginForm, RegisterForm, ForgotPasswordForm, logout control, ThemeProvider, branding loader (added on branch feature/platform-shared-auth-pages)
not_yet_present: no Django, Hugo, or maud path
no Dart token artifact, so the 8 Flutter repos have no shared route

waves.name: Make the layer consumable
waves.rationale: Nothing can be migrated until the package is on the feed and the schema is published.

Add a row to eng/package-manifest.json for the new package
Decide whether ui/feed tarballs are published to a public npm scope or vendored per repo
exit_criteria: a scratch repo can install the feed and import Button without copying source

waves.name: Prove it on one repository
waves.rationale: Adoption is currently zero. One real consumer proves the feed, the tokens, and the components work outside the owning repo; zero consumers proves nothing.
waves.candidate_rationale: Selected by measuring bespoke UI across all 34 dotnet repos in the undeclared-UI list. somodanote is the smallest that actually has auth pages to replace: 12 razor files, with hand-written Login.cshtml (42 lines) and Logout.cshtml (5 lines). Smaller repos were rejected because they have no auth surface to prove the replacement: singleatee (5 files, no auth), citylens (9, none), testify (11, none). The largest, openlearning at 234 razor files, is far too big for a first adopter because a failure there would be impossible to attribute.

candidate_state.blocker: The working tree has one modified tracked file, src/SomadaNote.Api/Dockerfile, which is leftover .NET 8 to 10 migration work (sdk:8.0 to 10.0, aspnet:8.0 to 10.0, plus ENV HUSKY=0). It is unverified and was not written by this effort, so the standard no-uncommitted-tracked-changes guard would block the migration. The owner must land or discard it first.

open_decisions.question: Publish the feed to a public npm scope, or vendor per repository?
open_decisions.why_it_matters: dotnet-platform-libs is now PUBLIC on GitHub, but the feed tarballs are committed to the repo rather than published. Vendoring keeps the packages private but means every consumer copies tarballs and no version bump propagates.
open_decisions.default_if_unanswered: vendor, because publishing a package under the user's npm identity is an account-level action the owner should take deliberately

ruling.reason: The feed tarballs are already committed under ui/feed/ and verified by verify-ui-feed.mjs. Publishing to a public npm scope is an account-level action under the owner's npm identity; a vendored feed with a sync script keeps every install offline-reproducible and digest-pinned, which is what the layer was built for. A consumer syncs with one script and never needs credentials.

open_decisions.question: Does the auth page set include a username/password form, or only provider redirects?
open_decisions.why_it_matters: forge's portal-browser-sign-in designs OIDC with PKCE only. The React pages assume a local form. The two must agree or consumers will get the wrong page.
open_decisions.default_if_unanswered: support both; a local form for site users, a provider redirect for operators

ruling.reason: react-auth ships a local username/password form for site users; forge's portal-browser-sign-in ships a provider redirect for operators. These are different actors, not competing designs. A site user logs in with a local credential; an operator authenticates to the control plane through OIDC with PKCE.

open_decisions.question: Are the 8 Flutter repositories in scope at all?
open_decisions.why_it_matters: There is no Dart token artifact. Supporting them means writing and maintaining a fourth consumer path.
open_decisions.default_if_unanswered: out of scope, recorded as a permanent exemption so they stop being counted as drift

ruling.reason: There is no Dart token artifact and writing a fourth consumer path for 8 repositories is not justified against the measured benefit. Record these as exempt so they stop being counted as drift rather than carrying an open gap forever.

open_decisions.question: Who owns branding.json — the repo, or the workspace registry?
open_decisions.why_it_matters: If the registry owns it, a product cannot change its own logo without a governance round trip. If the repo owns it, 70+ files drift again and nothing enforces a schema.
open_decisions.default_if_unanswered: repo owns it, schema validated at build time by verify-ui.mjs

ruling.reason: A product must be able to change its own logo without a governance round trip. The schema in ui/schemas/branding.schema.json and the loader in react-auth/src/branding.ts already implement this; verify-ui.mjs validates the shape at build time, so 70+ files cannot silently drift.
